statements.statement: An idempotent operation will yield different outcomes when executed multiple times.
statements.explanation: An idempotent operation produces the same outcome no matter how many times it is executed. This is the core principle of idempotency.

statements.statement: POST is an idempotent HTTP verb.
statements.explanation: POST is not idempotent because executing it multiple times can create multiple resources or have different outcomes each time the request is processed.

statements.statement: Repeatedly calling a DELETE request on the same resource won't change the outcome after the first successful operation.
statements.explanation: Once a resource is deleted with a DELETE request, subsequent DELETE requests on the same resource will have no effect, maintaining the outcome as the resource no longer exists.

statements.statement: GET requests are idempotent because they do not modify any resources.
statements.explanation: GET is idempotent because it only retrieves data and does not alter the server state, so repeated GET requests yield the same result without side effects.
